scenes.tts: Your nose hands the brain an orderly map, and the cortex scatters it. So what does the cortex keep?
scenes.visual: Title card: What the Bulb Sends. A tidy row of coloured glomeruli on the left; on the right a cortex sheet with scattered lit cells. The question appears on screen.
scenes.narration: Your nose hands the brain an orderly map, and the cortex scatters it. So what does the cortex keep?

scenes.tts: A smell starts with molecules binding receptors in the nose. Each receptor neuron makes one type of receptor.
scenes.visual: Olfactory epithelium with receptor neurons coloured by receptor type: red, blue, gold, green. Odour molecules drift in and bind some of them.
scenes.narration: A smell starts with molecules binding receptors in the nose. Each receptor neuron makes one type of receptor.

scenes.tts: Neurons of one type send their axons to the same small knot of synapses in the bulb. That knot is a glomerulus.
scenes.visual: Same-coloured axons converge from scattered neurons onto one round glomerulus each. Label: glomerulus.
scenes.narration: Neurons of one type send their axons to the same small knot of synapses in the bulb. That knot is a glomerulus.

scenes.tts: In mice, each receptor type usually has two glomeruli in each bulb.
scenes.visual: A mouse bulb outline with two gold glomeruli marked, one on each side. Caption: mice, usually two per bulb.
scenes.narration: In mice, each receptor type usually has two glomeruli in each bulb.

scenes.tts: An odour binds some receptor types and not others. So it activates a set of glomeruli.
scenes.visual: A row of glomeruli. Odour A lights one set; then odour B lights a different set.
scenes.narration: An odour binds some receptor types and not others. So it activates a set of glomeruli.

scenes.tts: Here is a question. Raise the concentration of the same odour. Do the same glomeruli light, or more of them?
scenes.visual: Odour A's set of glomeruli lit at low concentration. A concentration slider appears beside it. On screen: Same set, or more?
scenes.narration: Here is a question. Raise the concentration of the same odour. Do the same glomeruli light, or more of them?

scenes.visual: the question stays on screen

scenes.tts: Usually more. Higher concentrations often recruit extra glomeruli, though this can level off. So the set is characteristic at a given concentration.
scenes.visual: The slider moves up and extra glomeruli light around the original set. Label: characteristic at a given concentration.
scenes.narration: Usually more. Higher concentrations often recruit extra glomeruli, though this can level off. So the set is characteristic at a given concentration.

scenes.tts: The layout is a map of receptor identity. Where a glomerulus sits tells you which receptor feeds it.
scenes.visual: Each glomerulus tagged with its receptor colour. Label: map of receptor identity.
scenes.narration: The layout is a map of receptor identity. Where a glomerulus sits tells you which receptor feeds it.

scenes.tts: The layout is only coarsely related to chemistry. So it is not a fine chemical map.
scenes.visual: Two chemically similar molecules point to glomeruli that sit apart. Label: not a fine chemical map.
scenes.narration: The layout is only coarsely related to chemistry. So it is not a fine chemical map.

scenes.tts: Mitral and tufted cells carry the pattern out. Each sends one main dendrite into one glomerulus.
scenes.visual: Mitral and tufted cells rise beneath the glomeruli, each with a primary dendrite into one glomerulus and an axon leaving the bulb.
scenes.narration: Mitral and tufted cells carry the pattern out. Each sends one main dendrite into one glomerulus.

scenes.tts: Cells that send their dendrites into the same glomerulus are called sister cells. They share one input.
scenes.visual: Two cells under the gold glomerulus glow together. Label: sister cells, one shared input.
scenes.narration: Cells that send their dendrites into the same glomerulus are called sister cells. They share one input.

scenes.tts: Inhibitory interneurons sit around them. Periglomerular cells work in the glomerular layer. Granule cells have no axons.
scenes.visual: A periglomerular cell beside the glomerulus; a granule cell without an axon touching the lateral dendrites. Both labelled.
scenes.narration: Inhibitory interneurons sit around them. Periglomerular cells work in the glomerular layer. Granule cells have no axons.

scenes.tts: Mitral and tufted axons run on to piriform cortex, the main olfactory area of the cortex. There is no relay in the thalamus.
scenes.visual: Axons sweep from the bulb to a sheet labelled piriform cortex. A crossed-out thalamus box sits beside the path.
scenes.narration: Mitral and tufted axons run on to piriform cortex, the main olfactory area of the cortex. There is no relay in the thalamus.

scenes.tts: There the tidy map seems to vanish. One odour switches on neurons scattered across the cortex.
scenes.visual: Odour A's glomeruli light; in the cortex sheet, lit neurons appear scattered with no patch.
scenes.narration: There the tidy map seems to vanish. One odour switches on neurons scattered across the cortex.

scenes.tts: That raises four puzzles. Does the output of one glomerulus stay together in the cortex?
scenes.visual: A numbered list builds on screen. 1. Scatter: does one glomerulus stay together?
scenes.narration: That raises four puzzles. Does the output of one glomerulus stay together in the cortex?

scenes.tts: If it spreads out, how can the cortex still carry which odours are chemically alike?
scenes.visual: 2. Similarity: how is chemistry kept?
scenes.narration: If it spreads out, how can the cortex still carry which odours are chemically alike?

scenes.tts: Can a scattered pattern acquire learned meaning? And does an odour's pattern stay put from week to week?
scenes.visual: 3. Meaning: can the pattern learn? 4. Stability: does it stay put?
scenes.narration: Can a scattered pattern acquire learned meaning? And does an odour's pattern stay put from week to week?

scenes.tts: One idea answers the second puzzle. Where a piriform neuron sits tells you little about which odours excite it.
scenes.visual: One piriform neuron highlighted. Its position in the sheet is greyed out.
scenes.narration: One idea answers the second puzzle. Where a piriform neuron sits tells you little about which odours excite it.

scenes.tts: In our simple model, its glomerular inputs and its threshold decide its response. Real tuning also depends on input strengths, timing and the cortex's own network.
scenes.visual: Thin lines run from the neuron back to several scattered glomeruli, which glow. Caption: model inputs and threshold; cortical position does not enter this calculation.
scenes.narration: In our simple model, its glomerular inputs and its threshold decide its response. Real tuning also depends on input strengths, timing and the cortex's own network.

scenes.tts: Each neuron gets input from several scattered glomeruli. It fires only when enough are active together.
scenes.visual: Two, then three of the neuron's glomeruli light; the neuron fires only when enough are lit together. Label: simple model.
scenes.narration: Each neuron gets input from several scattered glomeruli. It fires only when enough are active together.

scenes.tts: So the more glomeruli two odours share, the more neurons they share, wherever those neurons sit.
scenes.visual: Odours A and B light overlapping glomeruli; neurons that respond to both appear scattered across the sheet. More overlap, more shared neurons.
scenes.narration: So the more glomeruli two odours share, the more neurons they share, wherever those neurons sit.

scenes.tts: With sparse responses, random wiring like this keeps the order of similarity on average. But related odours come out less alike than in the bulb.
scenes.visual: On screen: this model keeps the order; related odours come out less alike. Small caption: a prediction of this model, not a rule of all random wiring.
scenes.narration: With sparse responses, random wiring like this keeps the order of similarity on average. But related odours come out less alike than in the bulb.

scenes.tts: Anything tighter is not explained by this model. The cortex's own network and experience are the candidates.
scenes.visual: Recurrent fibres sketch between cortical neurons. Label: anything tighter? Not this model. Candidates: the cortex's network, experience.
scenes.narration: Anything tighter is not explained by this model. The cortex's own network and experience are the candidates.

scenes.tts: So the bulb sends a map of which receptors are active. The rest of this story is what the cortex keeps of it.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: The bulb sends a map of receptor identity. What does the cortex keep?
scenes.narration: So the bulb sends a map of which receptors are active. The rest of this story is what the cortex keeps of it.
